utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I would like to have a few minutes before 2.00 to address a procedural matter. So whenever you are about to change to another topic ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can interrupt here, Your Honour, if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. That will be good.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rendulic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- we'll end the hearing now. You will come back tomorrow morning. Tomorrow morning the hearing starts at 8.45, not at 9.00, at 8.45, but you will be informed by the services. I remind you that you are still under oath, which means that you are not allowed to discuss with anybody your testimony -- your testimony, and that implies also that you cannot speak to any of the parties. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The court usher will escort you out of the courtroom now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, the issue I would like to raise is your request to have additional time for the videolink witness on Friday. It's 056, I think; is that right? It's a -- it's a closed session witness so we don't --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- so we don't use his name. Okay. Mr. Stringer, are you aware of that and have you a view on the matter? Because as it is a videolink witness, we should take a decision in due course, so that's why I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In fact, we just -- I was putting together some notes and we were going to propose that the Prosecution could make its response orally in order to expedite the Chamber's consideration. We've taken a look at the Defence application. The Prosecution opposes it. Certainly based on the record that we have before us at the moment. The witness is a crime-base witness, if I can put it that way. There are two areas. One relates to Klisa, which is paragraph 29 of the indictment. The witness was also himself present and interrogated at the Erdut training centre. He -- the Prosecution will present his evidence pursuant to 92 -- Rule 92 ter and we'll be doing a 30-minute direct examination at the most with the witness. We think that on that basis, a doubling of the default time that would normally be available is not justified. It may be that when we see how much time is left, because we are somewhat mindful of wanting to finish the videolink witnesses in particular this week before we go into the extended period of non-sitting. It may be that if there's time and if the Defence is -- is in a position to persuade the Chamber that additional time is justified, perhaps it could be considered then at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just to know, Mr. Stringer, the next witness, which is GH-100, is that a videolink witness as well? That's an open-session witness, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No. The next witness is present in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Is in The Hague. Mr. Zivanovic, do you want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I understood that your question was related to the witness -- Witness GH-100. Not for the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Your request. We're talking about your request which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- about 56. And now my question was whether Witness 100 was also a videolink witness to which the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. I understood that he is -- I think he is videolink witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have that information right in front of my eyes at the moment. Actually, I might. I'm just ... I'm sorry, GH-100 is indeed a videolink witness, Mr. President. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: He is also a videolink witness. Okay. So, Mr. Zivanovic you wanted to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm in position to reduce my time for GH-056 to one hour. So the motion is moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So the request is moot. Okay. Thank you. That is settled, then. We convene tomorrow at 8.45. Please do not forget that we are 15 minutes early. Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of December, 2012, at 8.45 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.55 p.m.,
